newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES RALLY TO TOP TIGERS, CLOSE IN ON YANKEES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES RALLY TO TOP TIGERS, CLOSE IN ON YANKEES.

text.p: The Baltimore Orioles crept closer to the top of the American League East on Sunday, using three eighth-inning homers to rally past the Detroit Tigers 6-2 and cut the first-place Yankees' lead to three games.
Rafael Palmeiro and Chris Hoiles sandwiched two-run homers around a solo shot by Bobby Bonilla for the Orioles, who moved 10 games over .500 for the first time this season.
Baltimore remained one game behind the Whie Sox in the race for the A.L. wild card.
"We lost nine times trying to get 10 games over .500," Palmeiro said. "We needed that to get in the wild-card race."

With the O's trailing 2-1, Todd Zeile drew a leadoff walk against reliever Joey Eischen (1-1). Palmeiro lined an 0-1 pitch over the scoreboard for his 34th homer. On the next pitch, Bonilla drove his 26th homer over the wall against new pitcher Jose Lima. Hoiles connected three batters later.
"I don't think you call it an emotional high as much as surviving," said Orioles manager Davey Johnson. "I think all of us are kind of beat up and tired."
Alan Mills (2-1) pitched two scoreless innings in relief of Rocky Coppinger to get the win. Coppinger gave up two runs and three hits with 11 strikeouts in seven innings.
In New York, Ed Sprague hit a pair of homers and drove in four runs and Erik Hanson allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings as the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the Yankees 4-2.
Hanson (12-16) allowed eight hits, walked two and struck out four. He held the Yankees scoreless until the seventh.
Yankee starter Andy Pettitte (20-8) allowed four runs and six hits in seven innings, walking two and striking out six.
Sprague hit a solo homer in the second off Pettitte to stake Toronto to a 1-0 lead and added a three-run shot in the fourth for a four-run advantage.
Mike Timlin tossed a perfect ninth for his 25th save.
In Cleveland, the Seattle Mariners earned a split of their day-night doubleheader with the Indians.

In the first game, Charles Nagy (15-4) pitched a six-hitter, striking out 10 and ending Alex Rodriguez's hit streak at 20 games, and Jim Thome doubled in the winning run in the eighth as the Indians edged the Mariners, 2-1.
In the second game, Thome's error allowed Joey Cora to score in the ninth and Norm Charlton pitched 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief as Seattle edged Cleveland 6-5.

In Chicago, James Baldwin allowed four runs in seven-plus innings and Robin Ventura homered and drove in two runs as the White Sox remained on top of the chase for the A.L. wild card with a 7-4 win over the Boston Red Sox.
Baldwin (11-4) gave up nine hits and walked two with three strikeouts. Tony Castillo worked the eighth and Roberto Hernandez tossed a perfect ninth for his 37th save.
The White Sox took the lead for good, 3-2 in the fourth, when Tony Phillips' two-out single scored Norberto Martin.
The Red Sox opened the scoring in the third on Bill Haselman's RBI single and Jeff Frye's RBI double.
In Milwaukee, Bobby Witt threw a five-hitter and Mickey Tettleton and Juan Gonzalez slugged two-run home runs as the Texas Rangers whipped the Brewers 7-1.
Witt (15-9) walked two and struck out five.

Tettleton's two-run homer off Bryce Florie (0-1) capped a four-run third inning that was started by a solo home run by Darryl Hamilton, his fifth. Gonzalez added an RBI double before scoring on Tettleton's 20th round-tripper.
Gonzalez's two-run homer in the fifth was his 44th.
Texas leads the A.L. West, eight games ahead of Seattle, with 20 to play.
In Oakland, Tony Batista homered with one out in the bottom of the 10th inning as the Athletics overcame a 5-0 deficit in an 8-7 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
Hipolito Pichardo (3-5), the Royals' fifth pitcher, retired Terry Steinbach to open the 10th, but Batista hit a 1-0 pitch over the left-field fence for his fifth homer.
Mike Bordick added three hits and four RBI for Oakland.
Jim Corsi (6-0) walked three in the top of the 10th, but held the Royals scoreless for the win.
Jose Offerman was 4-for-4 with a walk and tied a team record with three doubles for Kansas City.

At Minnesota, Jim Abbott earned his first win since May 2 and Jack Howell started a triple play in the sixth inning and hit a solo home run in the seventh as the California Angels defeated the Twins 4-2.
Abbott (2-15) pitched six innings and allowed two runs on eight hits in his return from the minor leagues.
Troy Percival worked two hitless innings for the save.

After an RBI single by Marty Cordova tied the game 2-2 in the sixth, Ron Coomer hit a hard grounder to third baseman Howell, who started a 5-4-3 triple play. He then led off the seventh with his eighth home run of the year.
